title: Consilience of Inductions
description: Whewell's consilience: when independent lines of inquiry converge on one conclusion, confidence should jump — the inductions 'leap together'. The engine's core question is always whether the lines are truly independent.

demo.code:
import random
random.seed(1001)
n=6
# Evidence items: (source_id, supports). Shared-source items get discounted.
items=[("srcA",True),("srcA",True),("srcB",True),("srcC",False),("srcD",True),("srcE",True)][:n]
from collections import Counter
src_counts=Counter(s for s,_ in items)
indep_weight=sum(1.0/src_counts[s] for s,_ in items)
supports=sum(1.0/src_counts[s] for s,sup in items if sup)
opposes=sum(1.0/src_counts[s] for s,sup in items if not sup)
print(f"items={len(items)} independent_weight={indep_weight:.2f}")
print(f"supports={supports:.2f} opposes={opposes:.2f} convergence_ratio={supports/max(indep_weight,1e-9):.2f}")
print("shared_source_discounted:", src_counts["srcA"], "items from srcA counted once")
print("DEMO_OK")
demo.output:
items=6 independent_weight=5.00
supports=4.00 opposes=1.00 convergence_ratio=0.80
shared_source_discounted: 2 items from srcA counted once
DEMO_OK
demo.note: Runnable demo program verified by execution during the database build.

architecture: Evidence lines are registered with their methods and sources; independence is assessed pairwise. Converging independent lines raise the conclusion's grade; dependent lines are merged into one.
